title: A deleted post remains a candidate
description: A post is deleted, but its ID remains in millions of cached feed lists while fan-out workers are behind. The post record and authoritative visibility state already reflect the deletion. What should the feed service do when assembling a page?

options.text: Trust the feed list until its TTL expires because it was valid when written.
options.explanation: A candidate's old visibility is not permission to show it now. Fan-out lag must not override deletion or privacy state.

options.text: Re-check visibility during hydration, drop the deleted post and let the stale list entry age out.
options.explanation: The list is a derived set of candidates, not the authority on visibility. Read-time filtering keeps stale fan-out safe without rewriting millions of lists immediately.

options.text: Wait to acknowledge the deletion until every follower's feed list has been rewritten.
options.explanation: That ties a small authoritative change to enormous derived-cache work. Filtering on read removes that dependency.

options.text: Return the post only to users who cached its ID before deletion.
options.explanation: An earlier cached reference does not grant continuing access. It would make deletion semantics depend on cache history.
